story: Port MacKenzie, where the University of Alaska leased 829 acres to Terra Energy for the coal plant's industrial campus beside the borough's push for data center tenants (runner-up NSF $6M EPSCoR Smart Bio-Refinery using microbes and AI to pull rare earths from coal waste)

claims.claim: Terra Energy signed a 20-year lease with the University of Alaska for land near Port MacKenzie.
claims.verbatim: Terra Energy signed a 20-year lease with UA in late May, according to university officials.
claims.notes: In window. Identical text in ADN's October 6th republication (https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/mat-su/2026/10/06/large-industrial-energy-projects-planned-for-leased-ua-land-at-port-mackenzie/), a republication by permission and not an independent second source. The lease document itself is not public. Attribute to university officials quoted by the Mat-Su Sentinel.

claims.claim: The lease was signed in late May, according to university officials quoted by the Mat-Su Sentinel.
claims.verbatim: Terra Energy signed a 20-year lease with UA in late May, according to university officials.
claims.notes: UA's public comment period closed March 2nd (C24), so a late May signing follows it. The signing date is in no UA document fetched. The lease went unreported until October 6th.

claims.claim: The university land leased to Terra Energy totals 829 acres.
claims.verbatim: The 829 acres of newly leased university land could host a wide range of activities that fit that need
claims.notes: Corroborated by the primary UA notice, whose four parcels sum to 829.34 acres (C27 to C30, C32). UA's own land page (C33) gives 828.740 acres, a 0.6 acre difference on parcel MS.PM.0001.

claims.claim: UA Land Management director Adrienne Stolpe said the lease authorizes the Terra Energy Center Campus, which the lease describes as a large-scale industrial park.
claims.verbatim: The lease authorizes the development of the Terra Energy Center Campus, which is described in the lease as a large-scale industrial park.
claims.notes: Verbatim from Stolpe's email to the Sentinel, identical on ADN. Stolpe is director of the University of Alaska Land Management Office.

claims.claim: Permitted uses under the lease include facilities for industrial and commercial tenants and for energy generation, transmission, storage and distribution.
claims.value: energy generation, transmission, storage and distribution
claims.verbatim: Permitted uses include the development, construction and operation and maintenance of facilities supporting industrial and commercial tenants, energy generation, transmission, storage and distribution
claims.notes: Stolpe's quote. The article adds, in its own voice, transportation facilities, logistics and staging areas, warehousing and materials handling.

claims.claim: The lease authorizes Terra Energy to sublease to future tenants consistent with the permitted uses.
claims.verbatim: The lease also authorizes subleasing to future tenants consistent with these permitted uses,
claims.notes: Quote attributed to Stolpe.

claims.claim: The lease pays the university $20,000 in its first year.
claims.verbatim: Payment terms include a first-year payment to the university of $20,000, increasing to $60,000 annually in the second and third years.
claims.notes: Single-sourced to the Sentinel; the lease is not public. Attribute.

claims.claim: The lease payment rises to $60,000 a year in the second and third years.
claims.verbatim: Payment terms include a first-year payment to the university of $20,000, increasing to $60,000 annually in the second and third years.
claims.notes: Single-sourced. Same softening as C07.

claims.claim: When operations begin the lease payment would rise to $586,000 a year.
claims.verbatim: When operations begin, which is targeted for 2030, the payment would increase to $586,000 per year, with a 2% annual inflation adjustment through the end of the 20-year lease.
claims.notes: The article ties the $586,000 to the START OF OPERATIONS, targeted for 2030, not to year 4. Year 4 is 2029, the construction year (C11), and the article gives no rent for that year. Do not draw a rent step at year 4.

claims.claim: The $586,000 payment carries a 2 percent annual inflation adjustment through the end of the 20-year lease.
claims.verbatim: the payment would increase to $586,000 per year, with a 2% annual inflation adjustment through the end of the 20-year lease.
claims.notes: Single-sourced. Any compounded lifetime total would be a projection and must be labeled as such.

claims.claim: Site development and construction would begin in 2029, the fourth year of the lease.
claims.verbatim: Site development and construction would begin in 2029, the fourth year of the lease, with operation of facilities in the following years.
claims.notes: A plan, not an event. Say would begin or is planned to begin. 2029 as year four means year one is 2026, consistent with a May signing.

claims.claim: Operations on the leased land are targeted for 2030.
claims.verbatim: When operations begin, which is targeted for 2030
claims.notes: A target. DOE's page puts the coal plant's baseload power at 2031 (C39), a different facility and a later date.

claims.claim: Projects on university land are exempt from the best interest finding the state requires for major actions on state land.
claims.verbatim: projects on university lands are exempt from that requirement.
claims.notes: The full sentence on the page defines a best interest finding as 'an analysis of public benefits and costs that factors in public comment'. This is the Sentinel's legal characterization, not checked against statute. Attribute to the Sentinel.

claims.claim: Terra's full preliminary development plan provided to the university is confidential, according to Stolpe.
claims.verbatim: A full preliminary development plan provided by Terra to the university is confidential, Stolpe said.
claims.notes: Attributed to Stolpe.

claims.claim: Terra Energy officials did not respond to the Mat-Su Sentinel's request for comment.
claims.verbatim: Officials with Terra Energy did not respond to a request for comment.
claims.notes: True as of October 6th publication.

claims.claim: Information the university released about the deal does not highlight data centers.
claims.verbatim: Information UA released about Terra's projects does not highlight data centers.
claims.notes: Framing guard. The deck must NOT say the UA lease is for data centers. The data center link runs through the borough resolution (C41) and DOE's description of target loads (C40).

claims.claim: Mat-Su Borough officials were not informed before the university leased the land, an inholding within the borough's 8,000-acre port district.
claims.verbatim: Matanuska-Susitna Borough officials were not informed before the university leased the land, an inholding within the borough's 8,000-acre port district.
claims.notes: The article also says borough officials support Terra's plans but were blindsided by the lack of coordination. Present both halves.

claims.claim: Borough officials expect Terra to keep pursuing a lease of about 1,000 acres of borough land near the port for similar projects.
claims.verbatim: Borough officials at Port MacKenzie said they expect Terra will also continue to pursue plans to lease about 1,000 acres of borough land for similar projects near the port.
claims.notes: NOT an approved lease or agreement. The article calls what the Assembly approved a permit that functions as a placeholder ahead of any official lease agreement. RS 26-019 (C41) names designated borough lands with no acreage. Say Terra is expected to pursue, never the borough approved 1,000 acres.

claims.claim: If Terra requests and wins the borough lease, it would hold leases on about a quarter of the land in the port district.
claims.verbatim: If Terra requests that lease and the Assembly approves it, Terra would hold leases on about a quarter of the land in the port district.
claims.notes: Conditional and must stay conditional. 829 plus about 1,000 is about 1,829 acres, about 23 percent of 8,000.

claims.claim: Mat-Su Borough Port Manager Dave Griffin said the university leasing the land without any conversation with the borough "blows my mind".
claims.verbatim: it blows my mind," Mat-Su Borough Port Manager Dave Griffin said in an interview.
claims.notes: The full quote on the page reads 'The fact that the university leased it without any sort of conversation with the borough', then a dash, then 'it blows my mind'. House rules ban dashes, so render the two halves separately or with an ellipsis.

claims.claim: Terra's port projects are part of affiliate company Flatlands Energy's plan for a new coal-fired power plant near Skwentna.
claims.verbatim: Terra's projects near the port are part of its affiliate company, Flatlands Energy's, plans to build a new coal-fired power plant near Skwentna
claims.notes: Write AFFILIATE, not parent. The Sentinel's October 6th correction note clarifies that Flatlands Energy is an affiliate of Terra Energy.

claims.claim: The coal plant plan calls for piping carbon emissions more than 60 miles to Cook Inlet for underground storage.
claims.verbatim: with carbon emissions piped more than 60 miles to Cook Inlet for underground storage.
claims.notes: Single-sourced (ADN is a republication). DOE's page gives no pipeline distance or destination. Say Cook Inlet only.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska's land notice for the four Point MacKenzie parcels was posted January 30th.
claims.verbatim: Public Notice Start Date: January 30, 2026
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (before the window). The URL filename also carries 2026.01.30.

claims.claim: Public comments on the university's intent to lease were due by 5 p.m. on March 2nd.
claims.verbatim: no later than 5:00 P.M. on March 2, 2026, to be considered.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Read from the extracted text of the PDF (scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py). The same sentence appears on the notice web page.

claims.claim: The university's notice says the parcels will be leased at or above fair market value.
claims.value: at or above fair market value
claims.verbatim: Parcels will be leased at or above fair market value.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Appears on both the web notice and the PDF.

claims.claim: The university's public notice and disposal plan name no lessee and no proposed use for the land.
claims.verbatim: The University of Alaska intends to offer several parcels of land for lease at or above fair market value.
claims.notes: An ABSENCE, checked against the full extracted text of the PDF (notice, disposal plan, parcel table, two maps): no mention of Terra, Flatlands, coal, energy, an industrial park, data centers or any named party. The only intent stated is to offer several parcels for lease. Phrase it as the notice named no lessee and no use, not that UA hid the lessee.

claims.claim: Parcel MS.PM.0001 is listed in the notice at 369.34 acres.
claims.verbatim: Section 13: SWNW, Lots 2 and 3; 369.34 acres more or less.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. As printed, the notice's legal descriptions do not reconcile parcel by parcel (the Section 14 aliquots listed under MS.PM.0002 add to 320 acres, not 80). UA's land page (C33) resolves this: MS.PM.0001 is Section 13 SW4NW4 plus Lots 2 and 3 and Section 14 S2NE4 and SE4; MS.PM.0002 is Section 14 SW4NW4 and NW4SW4. Draw parcels from the land page's descriptions.

claims.claim: Parcel MS.PM.0002 is listed in the notice at 80 acres.
claims.verbatim: 80 acres more or less.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The PDF shows 80.00. Matches the UA land page (80.000).

claims.claim: Parcel MS.PM.0003 is listed in the notice at 60 acres in Section 23.
claims.verbatim: Section 23: S2NWSE, SWSE; 60 acres more or less.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The PDF shows 60.00. Aliquots check out (20 plus 40 is 60).

claims.claim: Parcel MS.PM.0004 is the west half of Section 26, listed at 320 acres, west of Port MacKenzie.
claims.verbatim: Section 26: W2; 320 acres more or less.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The PDF description reads 'This parcel is located west of Port MacKenzie just north of the Jeep Trail.'

claims.claim: All four parcels lie in Township 14 North, Range 4 West, Seward Meridian, near Point MacKenzie.
claims.verbatim: Township 14 North, Range 4 West, Seward Meridian, Alaska
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Sections 13, 14, 23 and 26, confirmed on the UA land page header.

claims.claim: The four parcel acreages in the university's notice add up to 829.34 acres, matching the 829 acres reported as leased.
claims.verbatim: 369.34 acres more or less.
claims.notes: DERIVED by arithmetic: 369.34 + 80 + 60 + 320 = 829.34. The notice prints no total. BLM's CadNSDI record lot areas for the same legal descriptions also total 829.34. UA's land page prints 828.740 (C33).

claims.claim: UA Land Management's Port MacKenzie page, last updated September 8th, totals the four parcels at 828.740 acres.
claims.verbatim: Total Acreage: 828.740 acres
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The 0.6 acre difference from the notice is in MS.PM.0001 (368.740 here vs 369.34). The page still reads as an open listing ('Applications will be evaluated as they are received.') months after the reported May signing, likely stale; no claim is made from that.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy lists Terra Energy Center Corporation of Anchorage for $89,000,000 in DOE funding under its coal recommissioning and modernization announcement.
claims.verbatim: DOE Funding: $89,000,000
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The page carries no date; date_of_source is the fetch date. The money funds engineering and design, not construction. Say selected for $89 million in DOE funding for engineering.

claims.claim: DOE puts the Terra project's total value at $190,375,155, including $101,375,155 in non-DOE funding.
claims.verbatim: Total Value: $190,375,155
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. 89,000,000 + 101,375,155 = 190,375,155. The value of the engineering project, not the plant's construction cost.

claims.claim: DOE describes the project as engineering and design of a 1,250 MW coal-fired baseload power facility with carbon capture in the Mat-Su Borough.
claims.verbatim: engineering and design of a 1,250 MW (target gross) nameplate-capacity, coal-fired baseload power facility with integrated CCUS, sited in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough of Southcentral Alaska.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. A target gross figure, five 250 MW circulating fluidized bed trains per the same paragraph. Say a planned 1,250 MW.

claims.claim: DOE says the plant's carbon capture system would capture more than 90 percent of its CO2, an estimated 8.26 million tonnes a year.
claims.verbatim: an integrated CCUS system to capture greater than 90% of the carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, or an estimated 8.26 million tonnes annually.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. A design target. Say is designed to capture.

claims.claim: The DOE-funded project aims to complete FEL-3 Class 3 engineering in 2027.
claims.verbatim: this project aims to complete FEL-3/Class 3 engineering in 2027
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. An aim.

claims.claim: The project description on DOE's page says it is positioned to provide baseload generation by 2031.
claims.verbatim: "The Alaska CCUS Commissioning Project is uniquely positioned to provide long-term, local, and price-stable baseload generation by 2031"
claims.notes: BACKGROUND and a PROJECTION in the project's own words reproduced by DOE. Say the project says it could provide power by 2031.

claims.claim: DOE's description names data centers among the loads the coal plant would serve, alongside utilities, military installations and critical mineral operations.
claims.verbatim: to multiple high-value load categories including utilities, military installations, data centers, and critical mineral operations.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The primary-document data center link for the coal project. The same paragraph says Cook Inlet gas is projected to be unable to meet utility demand as early as 2029; if used, attribute to DOE.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Borough Assembly passed Resolution RS 26-019, supporting a joint marketing effort with Terra Energy Center Corporation to solicit interest from large power consumers including data centers.
claims.verbatim: A Resolution Supporting A Joint Marketing Effort Between The Borough And Terra Energy Center Corporation
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Full title continues 'For The Promotion And Development Of Designated Borough Lands To Solicit Expressions Of Interest From Large Power Consumers For Data Center, Energy Infrastructure, Advanced Manufacturing, And Industrial Development Opportunities.' Status Passed; introduced 2026-02-18, passed 2026-03-17. The title names no acreage.

claims.claim: The Assembly overrode the mayor's veto of the Terra resolution on March 17th.
claims.verbatim: Assemblymember Fonov moved to override the Mayoral Veto.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. History entry dated 2026-03-17, action override the Mayor's veto, result Pass. The tally comes from C43. Original adoption 2026-03-03.

claims.claim: The veto override passed 6-1, with Assembly member Stephanie Nowers voting no.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly voted 6-1 during its regular Tuesday meeting to override Mayor Edna DeVries' veto, with Assembly member Stephanie Nowers voting no.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (republished from Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The override itself is corroborated by the borough record (C42). The same article says the resolution was first approved 5-2 earlier that month.

claims.claim: The resolution sets up a two-year partnership with Terra and does not require the borough to sell or lease land or commit to a data center.
claims.verbatim: The resolution establishes a two-year partnership between the borough and Terra, allowing the company to use borough staff time and resources. It does not require the borough to sell or lease land or commit to allowing a data center
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (republished from Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The article attributes the limits to a memo included with the measure.

claims.claim: On September 15th the Mat-Su Assembly unanimously passed a resolution saying large-scale industrial and energy development belongs at Point MacKenzie or West Susitna rather than on state land near Houston.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly finds that Point MacKenzie and the West Susitna region provide more appropriate locations for future large-scale industrial, logistics, transportation, energy, manufacturing, and resource-processing development
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The article notes the resolution does not specifically mention large-scale data centers. Do not say the Assembly asked for data centers at Point MacKenzie.

claims.claim: A $6 million National Science Foundation project joins UAF, UAA, Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: The $6 million National Science Foundation-funded project brings together researchers from UAF, the University of Alaska Anchorage, Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming.
claims.notes: Runner-up story. Release by Kate Avery, October 5th.

claims.claim: The project studies how microorganisms and AI-based methods can recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash.
claims.value: rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash
claims.verbatim: how microorganisms and artificial intelligence-based methods can help recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash.
claims.notes: Runner-up. Corroborated by the NSF abstract.

claims.claim: NSF's award record says the initiative is led by the University of Alaska Anchorage in partnership with UAF, Montana Tech and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: a use-inspired research initiative led by the University of Alaska Anchorage, in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University, and the University of Wyoming
claims.notes: Runner-up. UAA leads, PI Brandon R Briggs. Srijan Aggarwal leads UAF's portion only.

claims.claim: UAA's component of the collaborative award is $3,824,575.
claims.notes: Runner-up. Award start 09/01/2026, expiration 08/31/2030.

claims.claim: UAF's portion of the work is supported by nearly $913,000 of the total award.
claims.verbatim: leads UAF's portion of the work, which is supported by nearly $913,000 of the total award.
claims.notes: Runner-up.

claims.claim: NSF's abstract says the project applies reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin linked to microgrid simulators.
claims.verbatim: applies reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators
claims.notes: Runner-up. The AI substance.

claims.claim: UAF says the project is one of eight NSF EPSCoR projects sharing $39.9 million across 16 jurisdictions.
claims.verbatim: It is one of eight projects receiving a combined $39.9 million to strengthen research capacity across 16 jurisdictions.
claims.notes: Runner-up.

claims.claim: Srijan Aggarwal said the team is connecting environmental engineering, microbiology, mineral processing and AI to recover valuable elements from waste.
claims.verbatim: We're connecting environmental engineering, microbiology, mineral processing and AI to recover valuable elements from materials left behind as waste.
claims.notes: Runner-up.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Sentinel's report states rent for the first year, for the second and third years and from the start of operations, and gives no rent figure for 2029, the fourth year, when construction would begin.
claims.verbatim: Site development and construction would begin in 2029, the fourth year of the lease, with operation of facilities in the following years.
claims.notes: An ABSENCE, checked by the showrunner against every payment sentence in the article (the three quoted in C07 to C09 and this one). No sentence gives a 2029 amount. Say the report gives no figure for 2029, never that there is no rent in 2029; the lease itself is not public.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Sentinel published its report on the lease on October 6th.
claims.verbatim: on Oct 6, 2026
claims.notes: The byline line reads 'By Tim Bradner, Amy Bushatz on Oct 6, 2026'. Say reported October 6th, never first reported.

stories_surviving: Port MacKenzie, where the University of Alaska leased 829 acres to Terra Energy's industrial campus while the borough markets port land to data centers
NSF $6M EPSCoR Smart Bio-Refinery, UAA-led, using microbes and AI to recover rare earths from coal waste

killed.claim: DOE's page lists the Terra Energy Center as selected for negotiation.
killed.why: That phrase does not appear on the fetched DOE page, which is titled Project Selections and is undated.

killed.claim: The Mat-Su Borough approved an agreement covering about 1,000 acres of borough land for Terra and data centers.
killed.why: No fetched source supports approval of 1,000 acres. The Sentinel says borough officials EXPECT Terra to pursue a lease of about 1,000 acres. RS 26-019 names designated borough lands with no acreage, and its memo says it does not require a sale or lease. The surviving version is C18, hedged.

killed.claim: Borough record of the 1,000-acre agreement with date and vote.
killed.why: Not found. Legistar shows only RS 26-019 (passed, veto overridden March 17th) with no acreage.

killed.claim: Flatlands Energy is Terra Energy's parent company.
killed.why: The Sentinel's October 6th correction states Flatlands is an affiliate.

killed.claim: Rent rises to $586,000 a year from year 4 of the lease.
killed.why: The source ties $586,000 to the start of operations, targeted for 2030. Year 4 is 2029, the construction year, with no stated rent.

killed.claim: CO2 from the plant would be piped to Beluga.
killed.why: Beluga appears on no fetched page. The Sentinel says only more than 60 miles to Cook Inlet.

killed.claim: The coal plant will operate in 2031.
killed.why: Appears only as a projection quoted on DOE's page. Survives as C39 with hedging.

killed.claim: ADN independently corroborates the Sentinel's lease terms.
killed.why: ADN's October 6th piece is a word-for-word republication with permission from the Mat-Su Sentinel.

killed.claim: UA's land page shows the Port MacKenzie parcels as leased to Terra.
killed.why: It does not; it names no lessee and still reads as an open listing, probably stale.

killed.claim: Srijan Aggarwal and UAF lead the $6M NSF project.
killed.why: NSF's abstract says the initiative is led by UAA with PI Brandon R Briggs.

killed.claim: The Mat-Su Assembly's September 15th resolution called for data centers at Point MacKenzie.
killed.why: The Sentinel says the resolution does not specifically mention large-scale data centers.
